walkthroughs.body_html:
Use of Biological Resources — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Use of Biological Resources brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Use of Biological Resources.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How do decomposers return carbon to the atmosphere?
options: They respire — breaking down dead organic matter and releasing CO2.
Decomposers turn dead matter into oxygen and water, with no carbon involved.
Decomposers release carbon by physically breaking matter into smaller pieces.
PCR uses enzymes from bacteria to cut DNA into fragments, then sticks them back together.

mcqs.q: What are the three repeated stages of one PCR cycle?
options: Denaturation (high temp, strands separate), annealing (lower temp, primers bind), extension (Taq polymerase synthesises new strands).
PCR uses enzymes from bacteria to cut DNA into fragments, then sticks them back together.
Both introns and exons are removed and the cell uses just the cap and tail.
PCR has just one stage — heating the DNA until it copies itself.

mcqs.q: After pre-mRNA splicing in eukaryotes, which sequences remain in the mature mRNA?
options: Both introns and exons are removed and the cell uses just the cap and tail.
Exons remain; introns are removed.
Introns remain because they encode the protein; exons are removed as junk.
